items.title: Skylark Labs and CMU Robotics Institute Launch Multi-Year Partnership to Develop 'Artisan' Robot Manipulation AI
items.summary_en: Skylark Labs announced a multi-year research partnership with the labs of CMU Robotics Institute professors Jeff Schneider and Zackory Erickson to develop Artisan, an AI model combining vision, touch, and force sensing to help robots grasp unfamiliar objects and perform complex physical tasks such as opening doors, turning valves, and operating tools. Both professors serve on Skylark Labs' technical advisory board.
items.source_name: Tech Times (reporting on CMU Robotics Institute faculty partnership)
items.notes: Industry-academia partnership announcement; ri.cmu.edu and any original CMU/Skylark Labs press release could not be fetched directly due to network egress restrictions during this run, so this item is sourced from third-party tech-news coverage rather than CMU's own site. No peer-reviewed paper identified yet -- early-stage collaboration announcement, not a published result.

items.title: CMU Robotics Institute Develops Robots That Predict Human Actions for Manufacturing Collaboration
items.summary_en: Carnegie Mellon University's Robotics Institute, including PhD student Ruixuan Liu, is developing technology to let an industrial robot capable of lifting heavy parts (e.g., engine blocks) also predict and adapt to a human co-worker's actions during shared manufacturing tasks. The multi-year effort has been supported by Ford's University Research Program.

items.notes: Ford-funded human-robot collaboration research; the original ri.cmu.edu research page/announcement could not be accessed directly due to network egress restrictions during this run. No peer-reviewed publication identified yet for this specific update.
